title.narrative: CSF_Updating the Nationally Determined Contributions of Bolivia
CSF_Uppdatering av Bolivias nationellt bestämda bidrag

description.narrative:
De nationellt bestämda bidragen (NDC) är ett konkret instrument genom vilket länder åtar sig att uppnå klimatåtgärder, liksom förbättringar när det gäller institutionell förstärkning, uppmärksamhet på sociala frågor och genomförande av ekonomiska åtgärder som möjliggör införande av större grader av effektivitet för nationell utveckling.
NCerna är kärnan i Parisavtalet (2015) och bör innehålla ansträngningar från varje land för att minska nationella utsläpp och anpassa sig till effekterna av klimatförändringar. Parisavtalet (artikel 4, punkt 2) kräver att varje part förbereder, kommunicerar och upprätthåller de åtgärder och resultat som de avser att uppnå.
Enligt Climate Watch Data från 2016 (de senaste tillgängliga uppgifterna) är den primära källan till CO2eq-utsläpp markanvändning och skogsbruk (LUCF) som står för 63% av de totala utsläppen följt av jordbruk (18%), energi, avfall och industriella processer. Utsläppen i Bolivia kommer främst från förändring av markanvändning, som omvandlar skogsområden till jordbruksplantager eller betesområden (båda står för nästan 81% av C02-utsläppen).
Bolivia har brister i uppföljning och rapportering av sina koldioxidutsläpp med avsaknad av en uppdaterad utsläppsinventering. Det enda offentligt tillgängliga officiella dokumentet är från 2009 och innehåller information för två år 2002 och 2004. Frånvaron av en uppdaterad NDC åtagande kan få konsekvenser för i) ett lands löfte att fastställa sina mål för att minska klimatförändringarnas negativa effekter; ii) utformning och genomförande av effektiva klimatförändringspolicyer, iii) deras tillgång till globala gröna fonder och klimatfinansiering.
Detta förslag syftar till att stödja processen med att uppdatera Bolivias NDC genom ett samarbete med den akademin, det civila samhället och den offentliga och privata sektorn för att uppnå en minskning av 50% koldioxidutsläpp till 2030.
För att uppnå detta mål kommer detta bidrag att genomföras i två faser: - Fas 1: oktober 2020 till januari 2021: Analys av den aktuella situationen och utvecklingen av ett bibliotek för lindrande åtgärder. - Fas 2: februari till oktober 2021: Kvantifiering av minskningspolitiken och modellering, kalibrering och uppskattning av ett makroekonomiskt verktyg för att mäta den ekonomiska effekten av mildringspolitiken i Bolivia.
Det förväntade beloppet för hela projektet är 3 miljoner kronor.

The Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) historically has been a concrete instrument through which countries commit to achieve climate actions, as well as improvements in terms of institutional strengthening, attention to social issues and the implementation of economic measures that allow the introduction of greater degrees of efficiency to national development.
They have been at the heart of the Paris Agreement (2015). NDCs should embody efforts by each country to reduce national emissions and adapt to the impacts of climate change. The Paris Agreement (Article 4, paragraph 2) requires each Party to prepare, communicate and maintain successive nationally determined contributions (NDCs) that it intends to achieve. Parties shall pursue domestic mitigation measures, with the aim of achieving the objectives of such contributions. The Paris Agreement requests each country to outline and communicate their post-2020 climate actions, known as their NDCs.
According to Climate Watch Data by 2016 (the latest available data) the primary source of CO2eq emissions is land use and forestry (LUCF) accounting for 63% of total emissions followed by agriculture (18%), energy, waste and industrial processes. Emissions in Bolivia come mainly from land use change, which convert forested areas into agricultural plantations or grazing areas (both account for nearly 81% of the C02 emissions).
However, Bolivia has been facing deficiencies in the monitoring of Bolivia’s CO2eq emissions with the absence of an updated emissions inventory. The only publicly available official document dates from 2009 and contains information for two years 2002 and 2004. The absence of updated NDC´s commitment can have implications in i) the pledge of a country to establish its goals to reduce climate change negative effects; ii) the design and implementation of effective climate change policies; iii) their access to globally green funds among some.
This proposal seeks to update the NDCs of Bolivia, considering a joint collaboration with academia, civil society and the public sector to achieve a reduction of 50% CO2eq emissions by 2030.
To achieve this goal, this contribution will be implemented in two phases: - Phase 1: October 2020 to January 2021: Analysis of the current situation and development of a mitigation action library. - Phase 2: February to October 2021: Quantifying abatement policies and modelling, calibrating, and estimating a macroeconomic tool to measure the economic impact of mitigation policies in Bolivia.
The expected amount of the whole contribution is 3 million SEK.

The overall objective of the contribution is to update the Nationally Determined Contributions of Bolivia. It is expected to work through a collaboration including academia, civil society and the public sector to achieve a reduction of 50% CO2eq emissions by 2030.

During the last two years, Bolivia has been facing several challenges related to the deterioration of its economy due to the COVID-19 crisis, in addition to facing important environmental problems such as increasing deforestation and forest fires in the last decade. Based on a collaboration between academia, civil society and the public sector, Conservation Strategy Fund (CSF) developed the first analysis of the economic impact of a set of measures to achieve the NDCs for Bolivia, considering a portfolio of sectoral measures prioritized according to a series of criteria linked to their cost-efficiency. It has been implemented jointly in collaboration with the Plurinational Authority of Mother Earth (APMT for its Spanish initials). This is the first such study to be carried out in Bolivia, prior to it there were no projections of the macroeconomic performance associated with GHG emissions or the mitigation measures considered by the country.
The main conclusion of the study using public data and through the formulation of sectoral and general equilibrium models have estimated that the measures presented in the NDCs were implemented, specifically in the energy and forestry sectors, the level of cumulative GDP would grow by up to 2,7% higher than projected by 2050, which represents, at present, an additional US$ 15.5 billion, also having a significant impact on the generation of net employment.
In addition, it is estimated that the cost of implementing the measures would represent 30% of Bolivias GDP. Finally, based on some sensitivity analyses, the study projected that delaying deforestation reduction targets in the forest sector would lead to an additional 830 million tons of CO2eq emissions by 2050, with marginal gains for the GDP. One of the main results from this analysis in general, as well as in terms of cost-efficiency specifically, is that for 2050, the greatest potential for reducing emissions is in the forest sector (with a 40% reduction in emissions compared to the BAU scenario).
Within the framework of the communication and dissemination activities of the results, two dissemination workshops were organized in the cities of La Paz and Santa Cruz. Audio-visuals Materials were prepared that summarize the main findings of the project and they were widely disseminated with key actors and the general public. Also, a scientific article that describes the methodological approach, the main results and recommendations has been published with the Bolivian Catholic University (LAJED, https://www.lajed.ucb.edu.bo/a/issue/view/46/49).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
